PHASE 1: VALIDATE CORE ASSUMPTIONS (Days 1–30, Budget: $300–400)
Target: One CrossFit box; segment: members actively training 4+ days/week, likely to consume protein post-workout.
Tactic: In-gym sampling event (1–2 sessions); distribute ~80 bars with simple QR code cards linking to direct-to-consumer order page (Shopify). Assign one team member to attend, speak informally with members, note feedback.
Metrics to track: (1) QR scans / order page visits from samples; (2) first-purchase conversion rate (orders / samples distributed); (3) repeat purchase rate at days 15 and 30 (% of first-time buyers who purchase again). 
Go/No-Go decision point (Day 30): If first-purchase conversion ≥ 12% AND repeat purchase rate at 30 days ≥ 15%, validate channel and proceed to Phase 2. If below either threshold, gym sampling does not justify full rollout; pivot to alternate channel (e.g., direct online community, Reddit, fitness blogs).

PHASE 2: SCALE WITH VALIDATION (Days 31–60, Budget: $1,500)
If micro-test results meet go/no-go threshold (first-purchase conversion ≥ 12% AND repeat purchase rate at 30 days ≥ 15%), proceed:
Tactic: Sample at two additional CrossFit boxes using identical protocol. Track same metrics (conversion, repeat purchase at 15 and 30 days). Do NOT commit budget to additional channels yet.
Go/No-Go decision point (Day 60): If both new gyms hit the same thresholds, channel is validated across multiple sites. If either falls below, gym model may be site-specific; pivot to online community channels (Reddit fitness communities, fitness blogs, email lists).

PHASE 3: AMPLIFY EARLY WINS (Days 61–90, Budget: $2,000)
If gym sampling validates, allocate remaining budget to:
(1) Referral incentive ($800): offer first-time buyers $3 off next order for each friend referral, funded from product margin, to fuel word-of-mouth at zero customer acquisition cost.
(2) Email nurture ($600): simple email sequence to repeat customers at day 15 and day 45, highlighting testimonials and new flavors (if applicable), to increase second and third purchase frequency.
(3) Contingency / pivot budget ($600): reserved for testing alternate channel (fitness blogs, Reddit communities, or micro-influencers under $50 per post) if gym sampling does not validate.

Pivot trigger (Day 30 or Day 60): If conversion or repeat metrics fall below 12% and 15% respectively at any validation gate, immediately stop gym sampling and shift remaining budget to online community channels (Reddit, fitness blogs, email outreach) with same $300 micro-test protocol.

DELIVERABLE (2): POSITIONING AND CORE MESSAGE

Product Positioning: Premium plant-based protein bar designed *for* serious fitness athletes, not 'health-conscious consumers.' The bar is positioned as athlete fuel — clean protein, real ingredients, no artificial sweeteners or fillers — in contrast to mass-market bars (Quest, RXBAR) which prioritize macro convenience over taste and ingredient quality.

Core Message: "Made for the athlete who actually tastes what they eat."

Why it wins with CrossFit/serious fitness segment: (1) They care about ingredient quality and body optimization more than casual fitness followers; (2) They are willing to pay premium price for products trusted by their community (word-of-mouth channels them toward recommendations from peers and coaches); (3) They have repeat purchase behavior — once a bar becomes part of pre- or post-workout routine, it's habitual consumption, not one-time trial.

DELIVERABLE (1) TARGET SEGMENT: WHY THEM

Target: Fitness athletes at CrossFit boxes and serious gyms (training 4+ days/week, actively managing nutrition and performance), ages 25–45, household income $50K+.

Why this segment picks our plant-based bar over alternatives:

(1) Ingredient obsession: This segment invests heavily in body optimization (coaching, nutrition tracking, premium gear) and distrusts artificial ingredients. RXBAR and Quest dominate shelf space but are perceived as 'chemical' or 'artificial-tasting.' Our bar offers clean, whole-food plant protein — a genuine differentiation that aligns with their values.

(2) Community recommendation bias: Serious fitness athletes trust peer recommendations and trainer advice over ads. Within a gym community, word-of-mouth from someone you train with carries 10x more weight than a TikTok ad. Sampling inside their gym leverages this trust directly.

(3) Repeat consumption behavior: Once a protein bar becomes part of pre- or post-workout routine, it becomes habitual. Unlike casual fitness consumers (one-time trial, then forget), serious athletes who like a product typically buy it weekly, creating high lifetime value from a single conversion.

(4) Premium price acceptance: This segment is willing to pay $8–$10 per bar for quality, unlike mass-market consumers who hunt for the cheapest macro. Higher unit price and repeat rate = sustainable CAC/LTV even in a small sample.
